# h3_k8s_cluster (Resource)

Manages a managed Kubernetes cluster (h3k8s) with its worker group `workers` (the node pool `default`; add more pools with `h3_k8s_node_pool`). `kubernetes_version` is upgraded **in place** (one step: a newer patch or the next minor; no downgrade), `control_plane_replicas`, `workers.replicas`, `workers.cpu`/`workers.memory_gi`, `autoscaler`, `maintenance_window`, `node_local_dns_cache` and `api_allowed_cidrs` change in place; `name`, `project_id`, `cluster_type`, `pod_cidr`, `service_cidr` and `workers.disk_gi` replace the cluster. `kubeconfig` is sensitive and stored in the state. Import: `<project_id>/<cluster_id>`. Uses API-key (HMAC) access to h3k8s (`api.h3llo.cloud/api/k8s/v3`): the key must list the project; scope `k8s:read` is enough to read, changes and the kubeconfig (admin credentials) need `k8s:write`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "h3_k8s_cluster" "main" {
  project_id   = var.project_id
  name         = "prod"
  cluster_type = "PROD"

  # Changing the version upgrades the cluster in place (newer patch or next minor).
  kubernetes_version     = "v1.35.9"
  control_plane_replicas = 3

  workers = {
    replicas  = 3 # in place
    cpu       = 4 # in place, together with memory_gi (rolling node replacement)
    memory_gi = 8
    disk_gi   = 50 # changing it replaces the cluster
  }

  autoscaler = {
    enabled  = true
    max_size = 10
  }

  # NodeLocal DNSCache: a caching DNS on every node (in place; the first
  # enablement on an older cluster restarts the Cilium agents one by one).
  node_local_dns_cache = true

  maintenance_window = {
    enabled      = true
    day_of_week  = "Sunday"
    start_hour   = 2
    auto_upgrade = "patch" # only patch versions; a new minor via kubernetes_version
    exclusions = [
      { start_date = "2026-12-20", end_date = "2027-01-10", reason = "New Year sales" },
    ]
  }

  # Who may reach the Kubernetes API (in place, no restart); [] = everyone.
  api_allowed_cidrs = ["203.0.113.0/24", "198.51.100.7/32"]
}

# Workers in a network of the project VPC: pods reach the project databases and VMs
# by private addresses. Omit network_id to get the platform default. Changing it
# replaces the cluster. A Service of type LoadBalancer with the annotation
# h3.io/lb-internal: "true" gets an address of this network instead of a public IP.
resource "h3_k8s_cluster" "in_vpc" {
  project_id         = var.project_id
  name               = "apps"
  kubernetes_version = "v1.36.5"
  network_id         = h3_network.app.id

  workers = {
    replicas  = 2
    cpu       = 2
    memory_gi = 4
    disk_gi   = 40
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `kubernetes_version` (String) Kubernetes version, e.g. `v1.35.9` (`1.35.9` is the same version). See the `h3_k8s_versions` data source for the versions of the platform. A change **upgrades the cluster in place** (control plane first, then workers), it never recreates it. Allowed: a newer patch of the current minor or the next minor; a downgrade is refused at plan time.
- `name` (String) Cluster name (Kubernetes DNS label). Changing it replaces the cluster.
- `workers` (Attributes) The worker group: the node pool `default` of the cluster (one MachineDeployment). Further pools with their own size, labels, taints and autoscaling are `h3_k8s_node_pool` resources; `workers` and `autoscaler` always describe the pool `default`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--workers))

### Optional

- `api_allowed_cidrs` (Set of String) Source IPv4 networks allowed to connect to the Kubernetes API, as network addresses with a prefix (`203.0.113.0/24`, `198.51.100.7/32`; at most 50). `[]` opens the API to everyone; when omitted the current list is kept. The cluster's own nodes and the platform are always allowed. Changed in place, without a restart: new connections are checked within about a second, established ones are kept.
- `autoscaler` (Attributes) Cluster autoscaler of the worker group (pool `default`) and the cluster-wide autoscaler settings; changed in place. Removing the block disables autoscaling of `workers`. The autoscaling of other pools is set on `h3_k8s_node_pool`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--autoscaler))
- `cluster_type` (String) `DEV` (default) or `PROD`; limits the control plane and worker replicas. Changing it replaces the cluster.
- `control_plane_replicas` (Number) Control plane replicas: 1 (default), 3 or 5. Changed in place.
- `maintenance_window` (Attributes) Weekly maintenance window for platform-initiated work; changed in place. Removing the block disables it. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--maintenance_window))
- `network_id` (String) ID of an h3ovn network (`h3_network`) of the project VPC: the worker nodes run in that subnet, reach the resources of the VPC (databases, VMs) by private addresses and go to the internet through the gateway of the network. Omitted = the platform default: the project network `default` where workers in the VPC are enabled for the project (it is created with internet access when missing), otherwise the shared platform network. A Service of type LoadBalancer with the annotation `h3.io/lb-internal: "true"` gets an address of this network instead of a public IP. Changing it replaces the cluster.
- `node_local_dns_cache` (Boolean) Enables NodeLocal DNSCache: a caching DNS server on every node. DNS queries of pods to kube-dns are redirected to the cache on the same node with a CiliumLocalRedirectPolicy; pods with `hostNetwork` and the nodes themselves bypass the cache. Changed **in place** (default `false`); the provider waits until the cache is `READY` (or `DISABLED` when turned off). The first enablement on an older cluster does a rolling restart of the Cilium agents. The platform refuses it with `NODE_LOCAL_DNS_UNSUPPORTED` when the Kubernetes/Cilium version is too old and with `NODE_LOCAL_DNS_CONFLICT` when the cluster already runs its own node-local-dns or a local redirect policy for kube-dns.
- `pod_cidr` (String) Pod CIDR; platform default when omitted. Changing it replaces the cluster.
- `project_id` (String) Project ID (UUID). Defaults to the provider `project_id` (`H3_PROJECT_ID`). Changing it replaces the cluster.
- `service_cidr` (String) Service CIDR; platform default when omitted. Changing it replaces the cluster.

### Read-Only

- `cluster_ca_certificate` (String) Cluster CA certificate (PEM) from the kubeconfig
- `created_at` (String) Creation time
- `endpoint` (String) Kubernetes API server URL from the kubeconfig
- `id` (String) Cluster ID
- `kubeconfig` (String, Sensitive) Admin kubeconfig (YAML). Sensitive; it is stored in the Terraform state, so protect the state.
- `namespace` (String) Platform namespace of the cluster
- `network` (Attributes) Worker network reported by the platform; null on platforms without workers in the tenant VPC. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--network))
- `status` (String) Cluster status (`CREATING`, `READY`, `UPGRADING`, `UPDATING`, `DELETING`, `ERROR`, ...)

<a id="nestedatt--workers"></a>
### Nested Schema for `workers`

Required:

- `cpu` (Number) vCPU per worker (2-128). Changed in place (rolling replacement of the nodes).
- `disk_gi` (Number) System disk per worker, GiB. Changing it replaces the cluster (the API has no update).
- `memory_gi` (Number) Memory per worker, GiB (2-512). Changed in place together with `cpu`.
- `replicas` (Number) Number of worker nodes, changed in place. With `autoscaler.enabled = true` the autoscaler owns the actual count: changes it makes are not shown as drift, and this value is sent only when you change it.


<a id="nestedatt--autoscaler"></a>
### Nested Schema for `autoscaler`

Required:

- `enabled` (Boolean) Enable the autoscaler

Optional:

- `balance_similar_node_groups` (Boolean) Keep pools with the same node size and labels at the same size (cluster-wide). Same notes as `expander`.
- `expander` (String) Which pool the autoscaler grows when several fit (cluster-wide): `random` (platform default), `least-waste` or `most-pods`. Takes effect on clusters with node pools (`h3_k8s_node_pool`); can also be set with `enabled = false` when only other pools autoscale. The API does not return it, so changes made outside Terraform are not detected.
- `max_size` (Number) Maximum workers (2-100); required when enabled
- `scale_down_delay_after_add` (Number) Minutes after a scale-up before scale-down is considered (1-60)
- `scale_down_unneeded_time` (Number) Minutes a node must be unneeded before it is removed (1-60)


<a id="nestedatt--maintenance_window"></a>
### Nested Schema for `maintenance_window`

Required:

- `enabled` (Boolean) Enable the window

Optional:

- `auto_upgrade` (String) What the window upgrades automatically: `minor` (default; the latest patch of the current minor, else the next minor, one step per window), `patch` (only patch versions of the current minor; a new minor only by an explicit `kubernetes_version` change), `none`
- `day_of_week` (String) `Monday` .. `Sunday`
- `exclusions` (Attributes List) Periods without automatic upgrades (up to 10, each at most 90 days, not in the past). Removing the attribute clears them. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--maintenance_window--exclusions))
- `start_hour` (Number) Start hour, UTC (0-23)

<a id="nestedatt--maintenance_window--exclusions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `maintenance_window.exclusions`

Required:

- `end_date` (String) Last day, `YYYY-MM-DD` (UTC, inclusive)
- `start_date` (String) First day, `YYYY-MM-DD` (UTC)

Optional:

- `reason` (String) Free text, up to 200 characters



<a id="nestedatt--network"></a>
### Nested Schema for `network`

Read-Only:

- `mode` (String) `vpc` (a network of the project VPC) or `shared` (shared platform network)
- `network_id` (String) h3ovn network ID when `mode` is `vpc`

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by "<project_id>/<cluster_id>"
terraform import h3_k8s_cluster.example <project_id>/<cluster_id>
```
